  "text": "The wall opened wide enough for the smell of toast.

His father made a sound the boy had never heard from him, small and angry, like someone finding a locked door in his own house.

Anne caught the key before it fell.

“Not yet,” she said.

Across the threshold, the other father stood. There was a nick beneath his chin, fresh from shaving. The boy remembered that nick. His mother had pressed a corner of tissue against it while laughing at something neither of them would explain.

“Which one comes out?” the boy asked.

Neither man answered.

Anne turned over a label. On its reverse, in his father's handwriting, was a date. Beneath it were two words: almost stayed.

The boy took another key from the box. Then another. The labels trembled against his fingers.

“Have I been here before?”

His father sat down on the floor.

Upstairs, a tap began to run.

“You don't remember when we close it,” Anne said.

“But he does?”

His father watched the pale place where his hand had been.

The other man came nearer, stopping just inside the room. He looked past the boy toward the hall, at the schoolbag hanging there, its strap repaired with black thread.

“How old?” he asked.

“Eleven,” his father said.

The other man nodded slowly.

From upstairs his mother called, “Are you two ready?”

The boy put one foot across the threshold.

“There's ice,” he called back. “By the bridge.”

The tap stopped.

For the first time, the man with the smooth hands looked afraid.

Behind the boy, every key in Anne's box turned once against the wool."
